questions.q: What is the training objective during pretraining?
options: Maximizing human preference scores on generated responses
Self-supervised next-token prediction over a large unlabeled corpus
Classifying text into predefined topic categories
Minimizing the distance between two responses to the same prompt
questions.explain: Pretraining is self-supervised next-token prediction (causal language modeling) over a massive, mostly unlabeled text corpus.

questions.q: What distinguishes SFT's loss computation from plain pretraining?
options: SFT uses a completely different loss function, mean squared error
SFT masks the loss so only response tokens are scored, not the prompt
SFT trains on images instead of text
SFT removes the need for a tokenizer entirely
questions.explain: SFT typically still uses cross-entropy next-token prediction, but masks out the prompt tokens so only the response tokens contribute to the loss.

questions.q: Which stage consumes the overwhelming majority of total training compute?
options: Alignment
Supervised fine-tuning
Pretraining
Tokenizer training
questions.explain: Pretraining operates over trillions of tokens and routinely accounts for 95% or more of the total compute budget across the pipeline.

questions.q: What does DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) optimize for, as opposed to standard next-token prediction?
options: The probability that a chosen response is preferred over a rejected one
The exact match accuracy against a reference answer
The number of tokens generated per second
The size of the vocabulary used during generation
questions.explain: DPO optimizes the model so that a 'chosen' (preferred) response becomes more likely relative to a 'rejected' response, without needing a separate RL loop or reward model.

questions.q: Why is a 'base model' different in behavior from a 'chat model,' even though both can share the same architecture?
options: The chat model has more parameters than the base model
The base model was never trained on any data
The chat model has been through SFT (and usually alignment), which shapes instruction-following and response format that the base model lacks
Base models can only generate code, not natural language
questions.explain: The base model is the direct output of pretraining and completes text plausibly but without reliably following instructions. SFT and alignment reshape that same architecture into a model that follows instructions and converses helpfully.
